tools.parser: stdlib struct: LC_SYMTAB/nlist_64, LC_SEGMENT_64; symbol range ends at next defined __text symbol

demonstrated: The 525 byte-rotation temporary is aligned to32 and the two zero-filling48-byte windows to64; the initial526 windows were all aligned to16.
Both compiled cores have a stack-canary check and only its cold failure call. No new hot gv_loadu, memcpy or SSE helper call appears.
Both compiled cores perform native128-bit transfers: Q-register loads/stores to the temporary and paired X-register LDP/STP for the unaligned selected16-byte window.
The clamp to31 is folded into existing caller count masking: the526 kernels have no extra clamp CMP/CSEL or branch.

ROTQMBY525 uses MOV pointer,SP plus BFXIL pointer,count,#0,#5;526align16 uses AND count,#31 plus MOV pointer,SP plus ADD pointer,pointer,count. Alignment>=32 permits replacing pointer low5bits; align16 cannot guarantee that bit4 is zero.

The original aligned48-byte temporary fits wholly in one aligned64-byte block. Align16 no longer guarantees this containment. This is a loss of a host-temporary layout guarantee, not a change to guest/ABI alignment.
hypotheses_not_proven: Cache-line or store-to-load forwarding splits may contribute to the timing regression. Actual stack addresses, cache-line size and hardware counters were not recorded.
The address-generation chain change may contribute to ROTQMBY latency; its share of the measured12.52percent cannot be derived from instruction counts.
Virtual-machine scheduling, code layout, register scheduling and timing noise may affect subnanosecond medians. They do not justify removing unfavorable measured results.
actual_core_disassembly_audit.recommendation: Restore the original temporary alignments32/64 within the common native API, keep stack protection and the efficient window algorithm, then measure the resulting immutable source. No performance claim until that measurement.

alignment_followup.measurement_scope: Matched before/after baseline525 versus final aligned backend within attempt5; no controlled16-versus64-only timing experiment

final_actual_core_audit.conclusion: All nine native byte-window callbacks retain original temporary32/64-byte alignment, Q and paired-X native transfers, and only the cold stack-canary failure call. ROTQMBY variants recover BFXIL address fusion. This is structural validation, not a timing or phone-performance claim.
